name: nanoKONTROL2
//: Measured on the hardware on 2026-08-31 with sysex-controls, which reads the whole scene off the device in one request. Every number below was confirmed rather than believed; see the note.

ports.note: one port, and everything comes out of it: eight sliders, eight knobs, twenty four strip buttons and eleven transport buttons, all as controllers on channel 1. It carries two names and which one you see depends on which half of ALSA is asked: the sequencer calls it nanoKONTROL2 _ CTRL and rawmidi calls it nanoKONTROL2 _ SLIDER/KNOB. One device, one port, two spellings, which is why the patterns above match on the model name and stop there

note:
Eight channel strips and a transport, and nothing else: a slider, a knob and three buttons per strip, which is the plainest control surface anybody makes. That plainness is why it is worth having a file for at all, since every number below is fixed and none of it needs a manual to use.

Measured on 2026-08-31, and it is worth saying how, because this file used to carry the opposite warning. It was written from Mixxx's mapping while the device was on order, since Korg's own parameter guide describes every setting and prints not one factory value. The device arrived and sysex-controls read the whole scene out of it: the mode page, all eight controller groups and all eleven transport buttons, page by page. Every number agreed. So the community lists were right, and this file now says so on its own authority rather than on theirs.

What the scene reads. Firmware 1.3. Global MIDI channel 1, mode CC, LED mode Internal. Every controller group takes the global channel rather than naming one, every knob and slider is enabled with a range of 0 to 127, and every one of the thirty five buttons is mode CC, behaviour Momentary, off 0 and on 127. Momentary is the one fact here the numbers do not carry: a button sends 127 when it goes down and 0 when it comes up, so it is a key with two halves rather than a switch that stays where it is put, and a light on the hardware follows the host rather than the press because the LED mode is Internal.

The numbers hold in CC mode and nowhere else. The device also has five DAW modes (Cubase, Digital Performer, Live, Pro Tools, SONAR) in which the same controls speak that DAW's own protocol and none of these numbers means anything. CC is the factory mode, it is the only one described here, and it is entered by holding SET MARKER and CYCLE while plugging the USB cable in. Everything goes back to factory by holding PREV TRACK, NEXT TRACK and CYCLE while it powers up, after which every transport button except CYCLE blinks.

The knobs are called knobs and the sliders faders on purpose, because that is the one thing in here the application acts on without being told: faders go to the mixer and knobs to the machine in front of you, so the eight sliders are the first eight tracks' levels and the eight knobs are the first eight controls on whatever panel is open. Neither is stored, and any link made by hand beats both.

The thirty five buttons are named and nothing more. A name is what turns a link list from CC 46 into Cycle, which is the whole of what a profile is allowed to add. The transport buttons in particular are not wired to the transport: this device sends plain controllers rather than MMC or Mackie, so a play button here is a controller like any other and has to be pointed at something.

It has no screen, so there is no screen block, which is the same thing as saying it has none.

One port on Linux. Korg's own driver presents extra ports named SLIDER/KNOB and CTRL on Windows and macOS, which are not described here because nobody has seen them from this application.

Sources: the device itself, read with sysex-controls (github.com/soyersoyer/sysex-controls). Korg's nanoKONTROL2 parameter guide for the modes and the resets. The numbers previously came from mixxxdj/mixxx res/controllers/Korg nanoKONTROL 2.midi.xml and agreed with the hardware in every one of the fifty one controls.
